reps.name: Nikko April
reps.headlineGap: Never seeds or asks for the five-star review, on any call — including two where the customer thanked him unprompted.
focus: Week 1: Five-star standard planted in the expectations block and asked for at every close.
Week 2: The power-bill question after every thermostat answer, with the rationale he already gives.
Week 3: Confirm the appointment and stop — no new detail after the customer has decided.

reps.name: Andrew Trujillo
reps.headlineGap: Plants no five-star standard and never asks for the review, on a return visit that plainly earned one.
focus: Week 1: Five-star seed in the expectations block and the ask at every close.
Week 2: Add the hot-and-cold rooms question to an otherwise complete required set.
Week 3: Zip It — no ranges, no margin talk, no price history once the customer has said yes.

reps.name: David Canales
reps.headlineGap: Leads with the department limit instead of the next step when asked about replacement, and asked none of the four required questions on either call.
focus: Week 1: All four required questions before the tools come out, every call.
Week 2: Lead with the solve — every replacement question converts to an offered day and time.
Week 3: The full expectations block on every door, plus the five-star ask at the close.

reps.name: Joe Mendoza
reps.headlineGap: Answers pushback with a fact instead of a question — one objection was accepted instantly, another was met by disowning the price.
focus: Week 1: Empathy plus one curious question on every objection; never quote a price that has not come from the report.
Week 2: The power-bill question after every thermostat answer.
Week 3: Five-star standard planted at the door and the review asked for at every close.

reps.name: Robert Silinzy
reps.headlineGap: Never asks for the review, including on the only complete closed call on the board, where the customer thanked him twice unprompted.
focus: Week 1: Ask for the five-star review the moment a customer thanks you in their own words.
Week 2: Run the full expectations block on evening and emergency calls, not just maintenance visits.
Week 3: When a second component is found wearing, make it a priced option rather than a warning.

reps.name: Cole Pantol
reps.headlineGap: Answers the replacement question with an offer to get information later instead of a booked specialist, and lets the findings review become an email.
focus: Week 1: Every replacement question converts to a named day and time for a specialist, on the spot.
Week 2: Present the findings report in person on every call; email is the copy, not the conversation.
Week 3: The full expectations block on maintenance calls too, plus the five-star ask at the card.

reps.name: Brandon Moreno
reps.headlineGap: Reaches the moment the customer concedes replacement and goes to write the report instead of booking the specialist to a day and time.
focus: Week 1: Book the handoff out loud, with a day and time, before the report is written.
Week 2: Thermostat setting and the power-bill follow-up on every intake, then reuse the number at the presentation.
Week 3: Add the approval promise and the five-star standard to the Spanish expectations block.

reps.name: Benjamin Wyllie
reps.headlineGap: No priced option ever reaches a customer on tape, and a fully stated affordability objection was agreed with rather than worked.
focus: Week 1: Recorder runs to the end of the call, through options, price and close.
Week 2: Every replacement recommendation gets an appointment attached in the same breath.
Week 3: One curious question after every objection — never agree and move on.

reps.name: Francisco Valencia
reps.headlineGap: Never promises that no work happens without approval, and never asks what the power bill costs at the setting he has just proved the system cannot hold.
focus: Week 1: Recorder runs to the end of the call, through options, price and close.
Week 2: The rooms question and the power-bill follow-up on every intake.
Week 3: The approval promise and the five-star standard on every door, not just maintenance calls.

reps.name: Andrew Alonso
reps.headlineGap: Lets an early replacement objection sit unworked for the rest of the visit, and skips the expectations block entirely on the shorter call.
focus: Week 1: Recorder runs to the end of the call; review one complete recording with a manager.
Week 2: The full expectations block at every door, including short and tenant visits.
Week 3: Answer an early 'I'm not ready' with empathy and one curious question, not with the evaluation.

reps.name: Mario Castro
reps.headlineGap: Second graded day running in which every recording stops at the intake, and the required question set slipped from complete to half.
focus: Week 1: One complete recording, intake to close, reviewed with a manager.
Week 2: Filter, rooms, thermostat and the power-bill follow-up, back in sequence on every call.
Week 3: Five-star standard planted at the end of the block and asked for at the close.

reps.name: Nathan Colquitt
reps.headlineGap: Three of the four required questions are never asked, and the expectations block is missing both the approval promise and the five-star standard.
focus: Week 1: Recorder placement checked before the knock and again after the outdoor unit.
Week 2: The four required questions added to the intake he already runs well.
Week 3: Approval promise and five-star standard on every call, then the review asked for at the close.

skipped.reason: Six-minute recording collapses moments after the intake; no gradeable customer dialogue captured.
A 35-minute call captured only a handful of usable lines before the audio failed.
Arrived at a rescheduled job; tenant and landlord mix-up resolved at the door, no evaluation performed.
Six-minute return trip to the same job to order a part; no evaluation or decision conversation.
